moduleTitle: Lesson 1 - Introduction to the API Scan
learningObjectives: Launch API Scan through Commander or the documented filesystem entry.
Scan supported files or URI definitions and distinguish simple messages from generated service operations.
Configure payload, parameters, headers and authentication and inspect request/response views.
Apply contract-specific HTTP methods and interpret response status without equating it with all assertions passing.

elements.description: Select API Testing > API Scan in Commander, or launch ApiScan.exe in %COMMANDER_HOME%. The Modules menu also offers Scan Application > Non UI > API Scan. These are current documented entry points, not an arbitrary executable-distribution guarantee.

elements.title: Prepare and scan
items: Choose an authorized environment and plan where exported artifacts should be organized. A Component Folder is an organizational choice, not a universal scan prerequisite.
Use File to scan supported local/shared-drive JSON, RAML, Text, WADL, WSDL, XML or XSD input.
Use URI to enter a definition address; configure required scan authentication/proxy settings through Advanced.
Inspect resulting operations or messages. Open and Save commands manage projects; this lesson does not certify automatic last-project reopening.

elements.description: For scanned service definitions, API Scan initially displays empty operations and generates them when selected. A simple file can be imported directly as a simple message; do not generalize the service-operation behavior to every scanned file.

Use Method, Endpoint and Resource together with Payload, Params, Auth and Headers. Inspect generated example data against the contract; it is neither guaranteed valid nor guaranteed to return an error. The Home menu Request and Response controls select the corresponding view.

elements.title: Independent creation-request example
items: Assume the sandbox contract defines POST /shops to create a shop; choose this method because of that contract.
Set endpoint/resource, valid input and required credentials in the documented location.
Run the message and inspect status, headers and response body.
Check expected shop data and any intended persistent effects. Do not equate a success status with all assertions passing.

rows: The request succeeded; inspect content and business expectations.
The request created one or more resources.
No current representation was found, or the server is unwilling to disclose one.
An unexpected server condition prevented fulfillment; this is an HTTP response, not evidence that no server was reachable.

bulletPoints: POST processing and PUT creation/replacement semantics are distinct; supported operations come from the service contract.
A network failure without an HTTP response is different from receiving an HTTP error status.

elements.text: Scan an authorized small API definition, generate one service operation, configure valid and invalid requests, and inspect response evidence. The original Academy video and exercise file require access and have not been verified; historical Shops_Post naming and token rules are not certified here.

examPitfalls.title: Generalizing service-operation generation to every input
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming every scan lazily generates an Operation when clicked.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Service definitions generate initially empty operations on selection; simple files can import directly as messages.

examPitfalls.title: Treating generated data as guaranteed valid or invalid
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Sending example payloads without checking required fields, credentials and constraints.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the contract and configure meaningful request data. Default content is not guaranteed to succeed or fail; GET content does not have generally defined HTTP semantics.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming POST always creates and PUT only updates
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Choosing a method from a simplified CRUD slogan instead of the operation contract.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: POST requests resource-specific processing; PUT can create or replace a target. Use the method supported by the actual operation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After scanning a service definition (not a simple message file), API Scan shows empty operations. How are the operation details generated?

options.text: All operations must already be fully generated immediately.
Select the operation to generate its details.
Export is always required before viewing any operation.
Operations can never have message content.

practiceQuiz.hint: The service-scan documentation describes deferred operation generation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For a scanned service, empty operations initially indicate available functions. Select an operation to generate it; simple-file scans have different behavior.

optionExplanations.A: The documented service workflow initially creates empty operations.
optionExplanations.B: Selection generates the operation in this documented service case.
optionExplanations.C: Export is not a prerequisite for generating operation details in API Scan.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An independent sandbox contract defines POST /shops as its creation operation. Which method should a new-shop request use?

options.text: GET
PUT
POST
DELETE

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the specified contract, not a universal CRUD rule.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The scenario explicitly defines POST for this creation operation. HTTP PUT can also create a target under other contracts; that does not change this endpoint definition.

optionExplanations.A: GET retrieval does not match the specified creation operation.
optionExplanations.B: PUT has creation/replacement semantics, but is not the method specified for this operation.
optionExplanations.C: POST matches the stated sandbox contract.
optionExplanations.D: DELETE does not match the stated creation operation.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After running a request, what does HTTP 200 OK indicate?

options.text: The resource was not found.
No server could be reached.
The request succeeded; expected business data still needs verification.
The request is still pending.

practiceQuiz.hint: Interpret the status separately from the test assertion set.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 200 indicates request success. Inspect expected response data and effects separately; 500 is a server-error response, whereas an unreachable connection can yield no HTTP response.

optionExplanations.A: 404, rather than 200, concerns a missing or undisclosed representation.
optionExplanations.B: A received 200 response is not evidence of no reachable server.
optionExplanations.C: This gives the status meaning without certifying all business assertions.
optionExplanations.D: 200 is a success response, not a pending-processing status.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which independent preparation helps keep exported API artifacts maintainable?

options.text: Plan their destination and naming before exporting.
Delete every existing folder.
Disable API Scan.
Always use a local file regardless of the definition location.

practiceQuiz.hint: Organization is useful but is not a universal mandatory folder prerequisite.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Choose a clear destination and naming strategy. The scan itself supports files and URIs and does not require deleting existing work or a specific Component Folder.

optionExplanations.A: Planning the destination and names supports maintainability.
optionExplanations.B: Deleting unrelated work is unnecessary and loses data.
optionExplanations.C: Disabling the tool does not prepare artifacts for maintenance.
optionExplanations.D: Choose File or URI according to the actual input, not a blanket rule.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A sandbox contract requires a credential for a request, but the tester omits it. What should they expect and inspect?

options.text: Guaranteed success because credentials are always optional.
A possible rejection; inspect the actual response and configure the required credential.
Guaranteed automatic insertion of last-session credentials.
An automatic method change from GET to POST.

practiceQuiz.hint: The contract requires authentication; exact error behavior is service-specific.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The request can be rejected. Inspect the response and supply credentials as the contract requires; the exact status/body and any credential reuse must not be assumed.

optionExplanations.A: The question explicitly specifies a required credential.
optionExplanations.B: This follows the contract while leaving exact rejection behavior to the actual service.
optionExplanations.C: The documentation here does not guarantee last-session credential insertion.
optionExplanations.D: Missing credentials do not define an automatic HTTP method switch.

quickRecap.value: Commander API Testing > API Scan or ApiScan.exe in %COMMANDER_HOME%.
Scan supported files or URI definitions; configure required access/proxy settings.
A service definition initially has empty operations; select them to generate details. Simple files differ.
Method, endpoint/resource, payload, parameters, headers and authentication are separate controls.
Follow the contract; POST is resource-specific processing and PUT can create or replace.
200 success, 201 creation, 404 missing/undisclosed representation, 500 unexpected server condition; assert business results.
